name: Lianyungang
title: Lianyungang UTM: Ore Carrier, Tanker and Bulk Ship Gauging
description: Thickness measurement at Lianyungang: holds, ballast tanks, decks and piping gauged on very large ore carriers, VLCCs, chemical tankers and bulk carriers.
h1: Hull and Tank Thickness Measurement at Lianyungang, Jiangsu
intro: Lianyungang, on the Yellow Sea coast of northern Jiangsu, receives very large ore carriers at its deep-water ore terminal, VLCCs and chemical tankers at the Xuwei petrochemical complex, and bulk carriers, container ships and grain ships across its port areas. It is also the sea end of rail corridors to Central Asia. Ships here are gauged during long discharges and berth waits rather than in dock. Atlantis sends a team out from India for each ship and fits the work to the agent's line-up.

highlights.h: Ore carriers on a long discharge
highlights.p: The ore terminal has received ships of the 400,000-tonne class since the end of 2023. Discharge on the largest ore carriers runs over several days, leaving swept holds and released ballast tanks available for measurement while the ship is still alongside.

highlights.h: VLCCs at the Xuwei crude jetty
highlights.p: A deep-water channel completed in 2022 brought the first VLCC into Jiangsu to discharge for the Shenghong refinery at Xuwei. Deck plating, deck piping and certified ballast tanks can be gauged during the stay as early groundwork for a CAP or renewal survey.

Lianyun, Xuwei and Ganyu lie along the coast but are run as one port. A team can move from a bulk carrier at one area to a tanker at another without a separate trip, provided the agent's line-up puts the two ships close together in time.

port.h: Lianyungang: deep water on the Jiangsu coast
p: Lianyungang sits at the northern end of the Jiangsu coast, just south of the border with Shandong, where the Yuntai hills and the offshore island of Lianyun give the old harbour natural shelter on a coastline that is otherwise low and silty. For decades the port's limit was depth, and the long dredged channels that now lead in from the Yellow Sea have changed that: Jiangsu's first channel for 300,000-tonne ships was completed here in 2022, a second phase followed, and work on expanding it again began in 2024. The approach is open sea with no locks or river passage, though winter northerlies over the Yellow Sea can make small-craft work at the outer anchorages difficult, and spring brings the sea fog familiar along this coast.

The port describes itself as one port with four zones. Lianyun is the original harbour, with bulk, container, grain and general cargo terminals, including the deep-water ore terminal where a 400,000-tonne class ore carrier discharged for the first time in December 2023. Ganyu to the north and Xuwei to the south are newer areas, and Xuwei in particular has become a petrochemical base, with crude, liquid chemical and product berths serving the refining and chemical complex built there. A smaller river port area makes up the fourth zone. The traffic mix that results takes in very large ore carriers and Capesizes, Panamax bulk carriers with coal and grain, VLCCs and Suezmaxes, chemical and product tankers, and container ships on intra-Asia routes.

Lianyungang also has a role few Chinese ports share. It is the eastern end of the rail corridor known as the New Eurasian Land Bridge and a logistics base for Kazakhstan and other Central Asian states, so cargo moving between ship and train is part of its business, including grain carried by rail in open-top containers. For ship inspection that matters indirectly: rail interchange and transhipment produce berth congestion at times, and ships waiting their turn at anchor gain idle days that can be used for measurement. Lianyungang is not a ship-repair centre on the scale of Zhoushan or the Yangtze yards, so ships that need a docking usually go elsewhere on the coast, and gauging done here becomes their pre-docking record.

facilities.h: Where gauging can be done at Lianyungang
p: Most measurement here happens at the cargo berths. On ore carriers and bulk carriers, holds become available as discharge advances, and the long stays of the largest ships mean several holds, the double bottom and the wing ballast tanks can usually be covered before sailing. At the Xuwei crude and chemical berths, the team works on deck, in machinery spaces where permitted, and in ballast tanks once they are certified gas-free; cargo tanks stay closed while cargo is being handled. Container ships at the Lianyun terminals offer a shorter window suited to deck structure, hatch coamings and scrubber discharge lines.

Anchorage gauging is practical for bulk carriers waiting for the ore or coal berths, reached by a launch that the ship's agent orders from the port, with the usual caveat that wind and sea in winter can stop transfers. For a docking, the ship moves on to a repair yard at Qingdao, on the Yangtze or at Zhoushan, and we hand that yard a steel estimate built from the Lianyungang readings, with each location marked on the ship's structural drawings so the same points can be measured again in dock.
list: Deep-water ore terminal at Lianyun — hold, hopper and inner bottom gauging on very large ore carriers and Capesizes after discharge.
Bulk, grain and general cargo berths — hold, hatch cover and coaming readings on Panamax and Supramax bulk carriers during discharge.
Xuwei crude jetty — deck, deck piping and certified ballast tank gauging on VLCCs discharging for the refinery.
Xuwei liquid chemical and product berths — deck, piping and ballast space readings on chemical tankers within terminal permits.
Lianyun container terminals — deck, coaming and scrubber piping checks during intra-Asia calls.
Outer anchorages — pre-docking or pre-purchase gauging on bulk carriers waiting for a berth, weather permitting.

context.h: Port state control and the industrial trades at Lianyungang
p: Port state control at Lianyungang is carried out by the China Maritime Safety Administration under the Tokyo MoU. The port's mix of large dry bulk ships and tankers means inspectors see a good deal of ageing tonnage in the ore, coal and crude trades, where hold structure, hatch covers, ballast tank coatings and the fire main are recurring subjects. China's domestic emission rules add a consideration for scrubber-fitted ships, since open-loop discharge is restricted in port waters and parts of the coast; a scrubber left idle at the berth is a convenient system to inspect, and operators should check the current rules before arrival.

Tankers serving Xuwei face the vetting regimes of the refinery's suppliers and charterers, and an older VLCC or Suezmax is expected to show documented structural condition, often a CAP rating, before it is fixed. For the ore trade the pressure sits at the other end of a ship's working life: very large ore carriers and Capesizes that have spent years carrying iron ore develop wear in hold structure, and owners deciding whether a ship goes through its fourth renewal survey want a measured view of the steel required before committing to a yard. Readings taken during a discharge at Lianyungang serve both needs.

jobs.p: At Lianyungang the windows come from discharge and waiting time rather than yard stays. Superintendents of ore carriers and bulk carriers use the days alongside to measure holds and ballast tanks before a renewal survey or to follow up known wastage; tanker managers start CAP or vetting preparation at the Xuwei jetty; and buyers inspect bulk carriers that are discharging or waiting here. Container ship work is usually confined to scrubber lines and deck structure on a scheduled call. All of it is planned around the agent's line-up, which can shift as berths open and as rail-connected cargo moves through the port.
list: Hold, hopper and inner bottom gauging on a very large ore carrier at the deep-water ore terminal, as each hold is swept.
Deck, deck piping and ballast tank gauging on a VLCC discharging at Xuwei, as the first stage of a CAP programme completed later in dock.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a Capesize waiting at the Lianyungang anchorage for the ore berth.
Hatch cover, coaming and hold frame readings on a Panamax discharging grain, ahead of its intermediate survey.
Wash-water and overboard piping checks on a scrubber-fitted container ship during its scheduled call.

logistics: Lianyungang Huaguoshan International Airport serves the city with domestic and some regional flights, and most teams connect through Shanghai or Beijing; high-speed rail from Shanghai or Nanjing is an alternative for the final leg. Port passes for the ore, container and Xuwei terminals, and any launch to the anchorage, are arranged through the ship's agent, and the petrochemical area adds its own safety induction. Each technician from India needs a Chinese business visa supported by an invitation letter, so we begin the application once the expected berthing is known.

faqs.q: Is a discharge at the Lianyungang ore terminal long enough for hold gauging?
faqs.a: Usually, for a defined scope. Discharging the largest ore carriers takes several days, and holds are released in sequence once swept. We measure tank top, hopper slopes and lower frames hold by hold, then ballast tanks as the ship ballasts for departure. A full renewal-survey extent is larger than one discharge allows, so we agree priorities with the superintendent and leave the remainder for the yard.

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a VLCC at the Xuwei crude jetty?
faqs.a: Deck plating, deck longitudinals reachable from above, cargo and ballast deck piping, and ballast tanks once certified gas-free and released by the master. Cargo tanks stay closed while the ship is discharging. Everything is done under the terminal's permit system with instruments accepted for the area, and the results form the first part of a CAP or renewal gauging finished in dock.

faqs.q: Is there a ship-repair yard at Lianyungang for steel renewal?
faqs.a: Not on the scale owners of large ships usually need. Ships calling here generally dock at Qingdao, at the Yangtze yards around Nantong and Jiangyin, or at Zhoushan. Pre-docking gauging during a Lianyungang call therefore pays off: the yard receives a measured steel estimate in advance, and the class surveyor sees the same measurement points checked again in dock.

faqs.q: Can anchorage gauging be done off Lianyungang in winter?
faqs.a: On calmer days. Winter northerlies over the Yellow Sea can stop launch transfers, and the outer anchorages are exposed. For a ship waiting in winter we plan the work so the most important spaces can be measured on the first workable day, and anything left goes to the berth stay, where discharge provides a more reliable window.
